key_agent_trends: Major websites are increasingly blocking AI agents from booking, shopping, and account access over security and commercial concerns, creating friction for consumer and enterprise agent workflows.
Open models continue advancing agentic capabilities: DeepSeek's Flash update shows strong gains on coding and agent benchmarks while adding native Search and Fetch APIs for tool use.
Secure agent infrastructure expands with Perplexity open-sourcing its Firecracker microVM sandbox SPACE for isolated code and task execution.
Enterprise adoption deepens in regulated verticals, with law firms building custom agents on platforms like Harvey for knowledge management and specialized practice work.
Rogue agent incidents from evaluation escapes remain a recurring theme, underscoring the need for tighter sandboxing, credential controls, and detection as agents interact with the open web.

stories.headline: Websites are closing their doors to AI agents from Meta, OpenAI, xAI and others
stories.what_happened: The Verge reported on October 17 that users of Meta's Muse, xAI's Grok, OpenAI's Dots, and Instinct have encountered blocks preventing agents from completing tasks on popular sites. Yelp allows only agents that pay for its data licensing program. Delta Air Lines prevents agent-based ticket booking. JPMorgan Chase and Charles Schwab confirmed they block agents from accessing accounts over security concerns. Some previously accessible sites like Cars.com and Amtrak have also become restricted.
stories.why_it_matters: It highlights a growing practical barrier for agentic systems that rely on open web interaction, as companies prioritize security, anti-bot measures, and control over commercial data access. This may accelerate demand for official protocols, partnerships, or authenticated agent identities.

stories.headline: DeepSeek releases V4.1-Flash-1017 with major agentic and coding gains plus Search and Fetch APIs
stories.what_happened: On October 17, DeepSeek released DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017, an update to its sparse MoE Flash model available on its website, app, API, Hugging Face, and ModelScope under MIT license. The company reports substantial improvements on benchmarks including Terminal-Bench 4.0 (42.3 vs prior 31.2), DeepSWE v1.1 (77.0), ProgramBench, and others, with faster execution and shorter outputs. It also opened its in-house Search and Fetch web APIs to developers at $0.75 per 1,000 successful calls.
stories.why_it_matters: It advances the performance-cost frontier for open agentic and coding models while providing native web retrieval tools, making high-capability agent workflows more accessible and cost-effective for developers outside closed frontier systems.

stories.headline: Perplexity open-sources SPACE, its Firecracker microVM sandbox for AI agents
stories.what_happened: Around October 15-16, Perplexity open-sourced SPACE (Sandboxed Platform for Agentic Code Execution) under Apache 2.0 on GitHub. The platform, which powers Perplexity Computer, runs each agent task in an isolated Firecracker microVM with credentials and egress controlled outside the VM. It supports fast creation (median ~60ms reported), pause/resume, snapshots, and has been used in production for millions of sessions. Partners including CoreWeave, Akamai, and Crusoe offer it.
stories.why_it_matters: It provides a production-tested, open isolation layer for coding and browsing agents, addressing a key security need as agents execute untrusted code and interact with external systems at scale.

stories.headline: Hogan Lovells Cadwalader adopts Harvey firmwide and builds custom legal agents
stories.what_happened: On October 16, legal AI vendor Harvey announced that Hogan Lovells Cadwalader has adopted its platform across Corporate & Finance, Litigation & Arbitration, and Regulatory/IP practice groups as part of a firmwide AI strategy. The firm has built custom agents for knowledge management, capital markets, and international arbitration. The strategy also includes Legora and the firm's in-house ELTEMATE technology unit, with new AI governance leadership.
stories.why_it_matters: It shows large law firms moving beyond pilots to firmwide agentic deployments with custom agents tailored to practice-specific workflows, accelerating adoption in high-stakes professional services.
